notes: Built from t-table-erratic-01 (turn 1) and t-table-inaccurate-causes-01 plus the recertification note in t-table-erratic-01 (turn 2). Turn 2 - 'If it turns out to be that one, can we just swap it ourselves and carry on?' - carries no subject: 'that one' picks out the cable from the causes listed in turn 1 and nothing else identifies it. Shape is failure-mode-then-its-hidden-consequence, and the consequence is the interesting part: a cable swap is not a free repair because it can pull the sensor's certification with it. expected_to_favor is 'rag' - this lives in a troubleshooting table deep in the temperature chapter. Slice check: the source-of-truth and the four probe datasheets have nothing on erratic temperature causes and no notion of sensor certification or recertification at all, so a slice-bound arm has to guess, and the plausible guess (yes, just swap it) is the wrong answer.

turns.content: The water temperature on one of our pods has gone jumpy - it steps around by a degree or two between readings while everything else on the same instrument looks steady. Where do we start looking?

must_contain: points at the connections at the meter and at the sensor, either loose or dirty, as a first thing to check
points at a break somewhere in the cable
distinguishes this jumpy behaviour from a sensor that reads steadily but wrong, which points instead at a dirty sensor or an out-of-date calibration
must_not: attributes the jumpiness to real changes in the water without checking the instrument first
invents a numeric tolerance or drift specification for the temperature sensor
jumps straight to replacing the sonde

turns.content: If it turns out to be that one, can we just swap it ourselves and carry on?

must_contain: warns that swapping the cable is not necessarily a free repair, because changing cables can require the sensor to be recertified
states that the sensor must be verified or recertified before its readings are trusted again rather than being put straight back into service
notes that until that is done the readings from that sensor should not be treated as good data
must_not: says a cable swap is a simple field fix with no follow-up
invents a recertification interval, cost, or provider
confuses recertification of the sensor with a routine calibration of the other sensors
